answer.origin: BofA Research (Vivek Arya) relaying AMD's own internal estimates, as reported by Investing.com and syndicated on Yahoo Finance on 2026-07-22; AMD's underlying model and date are not disclosed in the article.
answer.note: Third-party relay of AMD's modeled claim that its EPYC 9965 (Turin) delivers about 2.4x the rack-level throughput of an NVIDIA Vera baseline in a modeled 100kW deployment, with the planned EPYC 6 (Venice) projected at about 3.3x. Because the figures are AMD's own estimates characterized by BofA, they support only the conclusion that AMD is actively marketing a throughput-per-rack metric against NVIDIA Vera; they do not establish measured NVIDIA CPU underperformance or any effect on NVIDIA revenue. If the metric gains traction with hyperscalers and enterprise buyers, it could pressure how NVIDIA's Vera CPU is valued on a standalone basis, though BofA itself argues NVIDIA's case rests on system co-design with Rubin GPUs and NVLink rather than per-rack CPU throughput.
limitations: The 2.4x and 3.3x multiples are AMD's modeled estimates as relayed by BofA; the workload, configuration, and assumptions behind them are not disclosed in the supplied record.
The Vera baseline configuration used in AMD's 100kW model is not specified, so the comparison cannot be checked against NVIDIA's own specifications.
EPYC 6 (Venice) is described as projected, and no availability or shipment date is given in the record.
The date of AMD's underlying estimate is not stated; the article's 2026-07-22 publication date does not supply it.
The record contains no NVIDIA response or independent benchmark testing the throughput claim.
follow_up: Retrieve AMD's AI 2026 Day materials and footnotes to identify the workload, Vera configuration, and assumptions behind the 2.4x and 3.3x figures.
Check NVIDIA's public Vera disclosures and any independent benchmarks for rack-level throughput at comparable power envelopes.
Confirm the Vera commercial availability timeline and whether NVIDIA has disclosed Vera customer adoption or attach rates.
Check whether BofA's underlying Vera or server CPU TAM report is available to verify the characterization of AMD's estimates.
